title: Intraoperative Anaphylaxis
triggerCriteria: Sudden hypotension, bronchospasm, flushing/urticaria, or angioedema after exposure to a drug, blood product, or latex.

steps.title: Call for help & stop trigger
steps.instruction: Call for help. Stop administration of the suspected triggering agent immediately.

steps.title: Airway & oxygen
steps.instruction: Give 100% oxygen. Secure/support the airway if compromised.

steps.title: Epinephrine
steps.instruction: Give epinephrine as first-line treatment — see Drug Handbook (Epinephrine) for dosing by route and severity, and follow your institutional anaphylaxis protocol.

steps.title: Fluids & positioning
steps.instruction: Give rapid IV crystalloid bolus for hypotension. Lay patient flat with legs raised if tolerated.

steps.title: Second-line therapy
steps.instruction: Consider antihistamines, corticosteroids, and bronchodilators per institutional protocol — these are adjuncts, not substitutes for epinephrine.

steps.title: Post-event
steps.instruction: Send serum tryptase (immediate + 1–2h + 24h per protocol). Document the suspected trigger and refer for allergy work-up.

title: Malignant Hyperthermia (MH)
triggerCriteria: Unexplained rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia, muscle rigidity, rising temperature, or dark urine (myoglobinuria) after a triggering volatile agent or succinylcholine.

steps.title: Stop triggers & call for help
steps.instruction: Stop all volatile agents and succinylcholine immediately. Call for help and declare an MH emergency.

steps.title: Switch circuit & hyperventilate
steps.instruction: Switch to a clean circuit/machine if available and hyperventilate with 100% oxygen at high flows.

steps.title: Give dantrolene
steps.instruction: Initial dose 2.5 mg/kg IV (up to 10 mg/kg until symptoms subside). Older powder form: 20-mg vials, reconstitute in sterile WATER (not saline — it precipitates), 2–3 mg/kg; newer rapid-dissolve form: 250-mg vials reconstitute as a suspension (full dose faster). Give via large-bore IV line. Repeat as needed; continue maintenance 1 mg/kg every 4–6 h × 24 h; total dose may reach 30 mg/kg.

steps.title: Active cooling
steps.instruction: Begin active cooling if temperature is rising (circulating water mattress/ice packs first; if insufficient, infuse 20 mL/kg refrigerated IV crystalloid, or peritoneal lavage if peritoneum open). Halt cooling at 38 °C to avoid overshoot hypothermia.

steps.title: Treat complications
steps.instruction: Bicarbonate 1–4 mEq/kg IV for metabolic acidosis (monitor gases/pH). Treat hyperkalaemia with bicarbonate, glucose + insulin (adult: 10 units regular insulin + 50 mL 50% dextrose), and calcium if severe. Maintain urine output >1–2 mL/kg/h (bicarbonate to alkalinise urine for myoglobinuria). Treat arrhythmias per ACLS; avoid calcium-channel blockers.

steps.title: Escalate & get expert help
steps.instruction: Contact your national/regional MH hotline (e.g. North American MH Registry 1-800-644-9737) if available, and arrange ICU admission for 24–48 h — recrudescence occurs in up to ~50% (usually within 6.5 h, up to 16 h). Monitor coagulation (INR, platelets, fibrinogen).

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 31 Neuromuscular Disorders and Other Genetic Disorders — Malignant Hyperthermia)

title: Local Anaesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST)
triggerCriteria: Perioral numbness, tinnitus, seizure, or sudden cardiovascular collapse/arrhythmia after regional block or local infiltration.

steps.title: Stop injection & call for help
steps.instruction: Stop injecting local anaesthetic immediately. Call for help and get the lipid emulsion kit.

steps.title: Airway & seizure control
steps.instruction: Give 100% oxygen, secure the airway, and treat seizures with a benzodiazepine — avoid propofol if the patient is haemodynamically unstable.

steps.title: Lipid emulsion therapy
steps.instruction: Along with basic life support and ACLS, give a rapid bolus of Intralipid 20%, 1.5 mL/kg ideal body weight (up to 100 mL in adults), followed by an infusion of 0.25 mL/kg/min (up to a volume of 200–250 mL). Redose per clinical assessment; continue infusion for 10 min after circulatory stability returns. Avoid propofol (lipid emulsion vehicle) in haemodynamic instability.

steps.title: Cardiac arrest modifications
steps.instruction: If cardiac arrest occurs, follow standard ACLS with these modifications: avoid vasopressin, reduce individual epinephrine boluses, avoid calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers, and be prepared for prolonged resuscitation.

steps.title: Post-event
steps.instruction: Monitor for at least 4–6 hours after a cardiovascular event (or 2 hours after a limited CNS-only event) per widely taught LAST guidance, and document the total local anaesthetic dose given.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 25 Local Anesthetics — Local Anaesthetic Systemic Toxicity)

title: Adult Cardiac Arrest (Perioperative)
triggerCriteria: Absent pulse / unresponsive with no normal breathing.

steps.title: Call for help & start compressions
steps.instruction: Call for help, start high-quality chest compressions (rate ~100–120/min, depth ~5cm in adults), and attach a defibrillator/monitor as soon as possible.

steps.title: Rhythm check
steps.instruction: Check rhythm every 2 minutes. Shockable (VF/pulseless VT) vs non-shockable (PEA/asystole) determines the next step.

steps.title: Shockable rhythm
steps.instruction: Defibrillate, resume compressions immediately, and give epinephrine after the 2nd shock, then every other cycle; consider amiodarone after the 3rd shock per standard ACLS sequencing.

steps.title: Non-shockable rhythm
steps.instruction: Continue CPR, give epinephrine as soon as feasible and every 3–5 minutes, and search for reversible causes.

steps.title: Reversible causes (Hs & Ts)
steps.instruction: Consider hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hydrogen ion (acidosis), hypo/hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, thrombosis (coronary/pulmonary) — anaesthesia-specific causes (high spinal, LAST, anaphylaxis, gas embolism) should be actively considered in theatre.

steps.title: Post-resuscitation care
steps.instruction: If ROSC achieved, optimise oxygenation/ventilation, treat hypotension, obtain a 12-lead ECG, and arrange appropriate post-arrest care/ICU transfer.

source.title: General adult cardiac arrest sequence, structured after widely-published ACLS algorithms

title: Laryngospasm
triggerCriteria: Stridor or complete airway obstruction with paradoxical chest movement, typically during light anaesthesia (induction/emergence) with airway stimulation.

steps.title: Remove stimulus & call for help
steps.instruction: Remove the stimulating trigger (suction, airway device) if possible and call for help.

steps.title: 100% oxygen & jaw thrust
steps.instruction: Apply 100% oxygen with CPAP via a tight-fitting mask, and perform a firm jaw thrust with laryngospasm notch pressure.

steps.title: Deepen anaesthesia
steps.instruction: If not resolving, deepen anaesthesia with IV or inhalational agent if the airway allows it.

steps.title: Break persistent spasm
steps.instruction: If obstruction persists with desaturation, give a small dose of IV succinylcholine (± atropine in children) to break the spasm and allow ventilation/intubation — see Drug Handbook for dosing.

steps.title: Secure airway & reassess
steps.instruction: Once ventilation is possible, reassess depth of anaesthesia and the plan for airway management before proceeding.

title: Septic Shock — Recognition & Resuscitation
triggerCriteria: Suspected or confirmed infection with hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg AND lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid resuscitation (or qSOFA ≥2 / clinical concern prompting urgent workup).

steps.title: Recognize & call for help
steps.instruction: Identify suspected source of infection. Call for senior help. Note time zero for the Hour-1 bundle.

steps.title: Cultures & lactate
steps.instruction: Draw blood cultures (before antibiotics if it will not meaningfully delay them) and send lactate.

steps.title: Antibiotics
steps.instruction: Give broad-spectrum antibiotics per local sepsis protocol/antibiogram as early as possible.

steps.title: Fluid resuscitation
steps.instruction: Give 30 mL/kg crystalloid rapidly for hypotension or lactate ≥4 mmol/L, reassessing for fluid responsiveness and signs of overload as it is given.

steps.title: Vasopressors
steps.instruction: Start norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor if MAP remains <65 mmHg during/after fluid resuscitation — see Drug Handbook (Norepinephrine) for dosing.

steps.title: Reassess & source control
steps.instruction: Reassess perfusion (repeat lactate, capillary refill, urine output, mental status). Identify and pursue source control (drainage, device removal, debridement) where applicable.

title: Sudden High Airway Pressure / Desaturation on the Ventilator (DOPES)
triggerCriteria: Acute rise in peak/plateau airway pressure, ventilator high-pressure alarm, or acute desaturation in an intubated/ventilated patient.

steps.title: Disconnect & bag
steps.instruction: If severe/acute, disconnect from the ventilator and hand-ventilate with 100% oxygen via a self-inflating bag — this immediately distinguishes a patient problem from a ventilator/circuit problem based on whether resistance is felt on the bag.

steps.title: D — Displacement
steps.instruction: Check for tube displacement (endobronchial migration, accidental extubation, cuff herniation). Auscultate for bilateral breath sounds, check tube depth at the lips, check capnography waveform.

steps.title: O — Obstruction
steps.instruction: Check for tube/circuit obstruction — kinking, biting, secretions, mucus plug. Pass a suction catheter to check patency; suction if secretions suspected.

steps.title: P — Pneumothorax
steps.instruction: Assess for tension pneumothorax — unilateral decreased breath sounds, hyperresonance, tracheal deviation, hemodynamic instability. If suspected in an unstable patient, proceed to emergency needle/finger decompression per local protocol without waiting for imaging.
checklist: Decompression performed if tension physiology suspected

steps.title: E — Equipment
steps.instruction: Check the ventilator and circuit — valve malfunction, circuit disconnection/kinking elsewhere, exhausted CO2 absorbent, ventilator settings entered incorrectly. Switch to a fresh bag-circuit if any doubt about the machine.

steps.title: S — Stacked breaths / Stomach / Spasm
steps.instruction: Consider breath-stacking/auto-PEEP (especially in obstructive lung disease — disconnect briefly to allow full exhalation), gastric distension splinting the diaphragm, and bronchospasm (auscultate for wheeze; consider bronchodilators).
